{"type":"text","text":"# Work unit U-0003

Rules: convert_raw_pointers_to_smart_pointers

## Files in the unit

### include/notes/store.h

```cpp
#ifnd

arguments.summary: Store now owns its notes through std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Note>> (private alias OwnedNotes) instead of a vector of raw pointers deleted by hand. create() builds notes with std::make_unique; the manual deletes in the destructor and in remove() are gone, as are the destructor and the private, undefined copy constructor and copy assignment that only guarded the raw pointers (Store stays non-copyable through its unique_ptr member). The public interface is unchanged: create(), find() and withTag() still hand out non-owning Note* pointers into the store.
review_notes: Kept raw, non-owning: the Note* returned by Store::create() and Store::find() and the NoteList (std::vector<Note*>) returned by Store::withTag(). They point into the store, which keeps ownership, so callers and tests are unchanged.

Store was non-copyable before (private, undefined copy operations) and still is, now because of its unique_ptr member; removing the user-declared destructor and copy operations makes it movable as a side effect, which no existing code relies on.
